ai.description: Leschenault’s Gecko reaches 13 cm. It is pale grey or brownish with irregular dark dorsal blotches and a white venter. Key features include a flattened body and smooth, non-protruding subdigital lamellae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus leschenaultii* is best identified by its smooth, granular dorsal scales lacking enlarged tubercles, distinguishing it from most other Indian *Hemidactylus* species.
ai.habitat: Leschenault’s geckos inhabit dry deciduous forests and rocky outcrops across the Indian subcontinent, frequently dwelling in tree hollows up to 1,000 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: Leschenault’s gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to hunt insects attracted to artificial lights on walls and buildings.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus leschenaultii* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, peaking during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: Leschenault’s Gecko is widely distributed across peninsular India, particularly in the Western Ghats and coastal regions, ranging from sea level to 1,000 meters elevation.
